lists.name: Pitchfork: The 200 Best Albums of the 1980s

podcast.body: Joe Jackson's fifth studio album, titled in homage to Cole Porter, was conceived as an LP entirely about New York City, where he had relocated in late 1981. Recorded in a small SoHo studio, it integrated the urban sounds of jazz and Latin clubs he absorbed in the city, alongside experiments with synthesizers and drum machines, influenced by Kraftwerk. The album became Jackson's biggest selling and most hit-packed LP, reaching number 4 on the Billboard album chart and reinventing his career by establishing him as an MTV staple and a critically acclaimed artist. "These sounds and styles would all wind up on Joe Jackson's fifth studio album. An LP all about New York City that he would title in homage to Cole Porter, Night and Day."
